title: Python package published to PyPI
appliesWhen: A Python library or tool published to PyPI (or another package index) for others to pip install.
ask: Will this be published to PyPI? Which Python versions are supported, is it pure Python or does it need compiled wheels, and is it typed?

sources.title: Python Packaging User Guide: Writing your pyproject.toml
Python Packaging User Guide: Publishing releases with GitHub Actions (trusted publishing)
PyPI Docs: Publishing with a Trusted Publisher
Python typing spec: Distributing type information (py.typed)

guidance: Use PEP 621 [project] metadata in pyproject.toml with a [build-system] table; name is the only field that cannot be dynamic.

licence: use an SPDX expression string (license = "MIT") and license-files (PEP 639). Older backends reject it; it needs hatchling 1.27+, setuptools 77.0.3+, flit-core 3.12+, pdm-backend 2.4.0+, poetry-core 2.2.0+ or uv-build 0.7.19+.
Set requires-python to the lowest version you test; avoid an upper bound. Classifiers are for search only and do not restrict installs.
Build the sdist and wheel once in CI with python -m build, check them with twine check --strict, and publish those exact files; build and publish run in separate jobs.
Compiled extensions need wheels for each supported platform and Python version (commonly built with cibuildwheel); otherwise users compile from the sdist.

Publish with trusted publishing (pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1, id-token: write at job level, a "pypi" GitHub environment with required reviewers). The action uploads attestations by default.
PyPI never allows a file name to be reused, even after deletion: a bad release is fixed with a new version (and a yank of the bad one).
Typed packages ship a py.typed file inside the import package so type checkers use the inline annotations; it must be in the wheel.
Check the release on TestPyPI first when changing packaging; PyPI requires 2FA on every account.

gates.title: pyproject.toml has complete [project] metadata
gates.setup: Needs Python 3.11+ (tomllib) to run the check.
gates.command: python3 -c "import sys,tomllib;p=tomllib.load(open('pyproject.toml','rb')).get('project',{});d=p.get('dynamic',[]);miss=[k for k in ('name','version','description','readme','requires-python','license','urls') if k not in p and k not in d]+(['license as an SPDX expression string (PEP 639), not a table'] if isinstance(p.get('license'),dict) else []);print('pyproject.toml [project] needs: '+', '.join(miss) if miss else p.get('name','?')+': [project] metadata present');sys.exit(1 if miss else 0)"
gates.architecture: Record the distribution name, build backend (and its minimum version), how the version is set (static or dynamic from a tag), requires-python, the SPDX licence expression and project URLs.
acceptance: pyproject.toml [project] has name, version (or dynamic), description, readme, requires-python, license and urls
license is an SPDX expression string with license-files, not the deprecated table form

gates.title: sdist and wheel build and pass twine check
gates.setup: python3 -m pip install build twine (in the project virtual environment or CI)
gates.command: rm -rf dist && python3 -m build && python3 -m twine check --strict dist/*
gates.architecture: Record the artifacts produced (sdist plus pure-Python wheel, or platform wheels and how they are built) and what the sdist includes.
acceptance: python -m build produces an sdist and at least one wheel in dist/
twine check --strict dist/* passes (metadata valid, README renders on PyPI)

gates.title: The wheel ships py.typed (typed packages)
gates.setup: Runs after G-PYLIB-BUILD; it reads the wheel in dist/.
gates.command: python3 -c "import glob,sys,zipfile;w=sorted(glob.glob('dist/*.whl'));ok=bool(w) and any(n.endswith('/py.typed') for n in zipfile.ZipFile(w[-1]).namelist());print('py.typed is in '+w[-1] if ok else 'no wheel in dist/ ships py.typed (run G-PYLIB-BUILD first)');sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)"
gates.architecture: Record whether the package is typed, the type checker and strictness used in CI (for example mypy --strict or pyright), and where py.typed lives; remove this gate for an untyped package with a reason.
acceptance: The built wheel contains py.typed inside the import package
The chosen type checker reports no errors on the package

gates.title: Versions follow PEP 440 and SemVer-style compatibility with a changelog
gates.architecture: Record the public API (what is importable without a leading underscore), the version policy, the deprecation policy and where the changelog lives.
acceptance: Each release has a PEP 440 version and a changelog entry
Removed or changed public API is deprecated first or released as a major version

gates.title: Releases are published from CI with trusted publishing
gates.architecture: Record the release workflow: build job, separate publish job using pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish with id-token: write at job level, the protected "pypi" environment, the trusted publisher configured on PyPI, and TestPyPI use.
acceptance: The project is published only from the CI workflow registered as its trusted publisher; no long-lived API token is stored in CI
The publish job uploads the files built by the build job and attestations appear on PyPI

gates.title: Package licence and dependency licence compatibility need review
gates.architecture: Record the chosen licence and the runtime dependencies (and any vendored or bundled code, including libraries linked into wheels) with their licences.
